implementation_summary: Created failed-welcomes.ts (IDB-backed log via createKVStore following the forgotten-slots.ts pattern). Exports appendFailedWelcome (upsert by giftWrapEventId — satisfies dedup AC-LOG-3), loadFailedWelcomes (with since/limit filters), forgetFailedWelcome, and pruneOlderThan. All four mutations dispatch notestr:failed-welcomes-changed on window (AC-LOG-4). failureDetail is capped at 500 chars. Wired two points in device-sync.ts: (1) joinFromWelcomeInvite catch block now logs the failure via appendFailedWelcome BEFORE markAsRead (AC-LOG-1), extracting groupId via readInviteGroupInfo if available; (2) inviteReader.on('error') handler now calls appendFailedWelcome with failureReason='decrypt_failed' (AC-LOG-2), fire-and-forget with .catch. Added pruneOlderThan call in useDeviceSync useEffect for AC-LOG-5. Added notestr-failed-welcomes to KNOWN_IDB_NAMES in cleanup.ts (AC-OBS-1). Added vi.mock('./failed-welcomes') to device-sync.test.ts to suppress IDB access in the test environment (remediation round 1).

mocks_introduced.reason: joinFromWelcomeInvite now calls appendFailedWelcome in its catch block; the test environment has no indexedDB, so the real store must be suppressed.

retrospective.harder_than_needed: The device-sync.test.ts regression (indexedDB not defined) required an extra remediation round. The test already mocked mls-trace and marmot-ts to prevent real I/O, but the new appendFailedWelcome call was not anticipated — it routes through the unmocked createKVStore, which hits real idb-keyval. The scope list did not include device-sync.test.ts, creating brief ambiguity about whether touching it was allowed. The correct decision was to add the mock there since the regression is directly caused by the production code change.
